Compares; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — no context file vs LLM-generated vs developer-written context files, 4 agent+model pairs, 2 benchmarks, with ablations; proposes the CTXBENCH benchmark (138 instances)

Context files (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md), no version (format 'formalized in August 2025'): (A) LLM-generated context file via each agent's recommended init command and model; (B) developer-committed context file from the pre-patch repository state

A single context file at repository root (CLAUDE.md for Claude Code; AGENTS.md for Codex and Qwen Code). LLM-generated files typically contain Overview, Tooling, Testing; developer files: mean 641 words, 9.7 sections, 8 of 12 have a codebase overview

Behavioural trace analysis: steps before first interaction with a gold-patch file; tool-use frequency and intent; instruction following (tool mentioned vs used); reasoning tokens; presence of codebase overviews in generated files

Automatic: tests in Docker, traces, cost logs; LLM-as-judge (GPT-OSS-120B) for overview detection and tool-call intent; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel, stratified permutation and McNemar tests. Manual: trace inspection, cheating check, review of all CTXBENCH instances and edit of 25 over-specified tests

Criterion: hidden tests pass. Values: success % SWE-bench Lite / CTXBENCH (Table 5, CTXBENCH rows labelled 'PLAN-BENCH'); cost USD per instance SWE / CTX (Table 2). One run each.

- Ablation (GPT-5.2 + Codex, LLM file without testing / overview / tooling, categories removed with GPT-5.4, Table 7): CTX accuracy 66.67 / 62.32 / 63.77% vs full 68.12%; SWE 57.72 / 54.20 / 53.69% vs 54.36%; none significant; cost CTX $0.3730 / $0.4027 / $0.4815 vs $0.4715, SWE $0.2756 / $0.3018 / $0.2715 vs $0.3272; removing testing lowers cost significantly on both benchmarks (p = 0.023 CTX, 0.0035 SWE), removing tooling on SWE-bench (p = 0.0012)
- Ablation (generating model, prompt, documentation removed): stronger models' files +2% SWE, -3% CTX; no consistent prompt effect; with docs removed LLM files +2.7% on average (Fig. 7, 8, 12 only)
Verdicts: quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors (all configurations)

Tasks: SWE-bench Lite (300) + CTXBENCH (138; LLM-generated task descriptions and tests, manually reviewed). Configurations: 4 agent+model pairs x {None, LLM, DEV}; DEV only on CTXBENCH (20 cells) + ablations. Baseline: None. Held constant: default agent settings, temperature (0 for Sonnet/GPT, 0.7 for Qwen), task, Docker image, git history removed, web access allowed. Acceptance tests: hidden tests (75% coverage; 25/138 edited). Repetitions: 1 (sampled once). Human intervention: none during runs; manual cheating check after

LLM vs None: success -0.5 pts SWE-bench (p=0.87), -2 pts CTXBENCH (p=0.37), drops in 5 of 8 settings; steps +2.45 / +3.92, cost +20% / +23% (significant). DEV vs None: +2.4 pts (p=0.21), +3.34 steps, cost up to +19% (significant). DEV vs LLM: DEV better (p=0.038). Text (p. 2) says DEV outperforms LLM by '7% on average'; Table 5 per-model differences range 0 (GPT-5.2) to 6.5 pts (Qwen3-30B), ~5 for the others. Reasoning tokens +22%/+10% (GPT-5.2/GPT-5.1 Mini, SWE) with LLM files

Distinguished configurations on cost and steps, mostly not on success. Repeatability: single sample per configuration, standard errors and statistical tests reported; temperature 0 for 3 of 4 models; no code/data release link found. Limitations stated: SWE-bench per-repo estimates noisy (django dominates); CTXBENCH ~15% easier than SWE-bench; contamination checked and ruled out; Python only

Python only (parametric knowledge may nullify context files); only task resolution measured (efficiency, security future work); how to generate useful context files is open. Recommends omitting LLM-generated files and keeping human files to non-standard instructions

Same study as pilot record P2 (author verified Table 5 Sonnet values, one run, the '7%' inconsistency and affiliations, 2026-11-11). Table 5 labels CTXBENCH rows 'PLAN-BENCH'.
